what: The acceptance list of completion task 3.8 (spec R5): 26 S&P 500 ever-members that stopped trading -- 11 failures (bankruptcy, seizure, conservatorship) and 15 acquisitions (one of them Bear Stearns, sold at about $10 after a near-collapse) -- with the last trading date, the reason, and the notice each date was read from. tools/accept_delisted.py asks the delisted-names source for each and passes at 24 of 26.
method: Each date was looked up on 2026-11-20 by web search of the exchange's (NYSE Form 25 notices on EDGAR, Nasdaq trader alerts), the SEC's, the regulator's or the company's own pages; source_url is the page used. date_basis is 'stated' when the page gives the last trading date or says trading ended after that session's close, and 'inferred: ...' when the page gives a suspension or halt before an open and the date is the session before it (the acceptance test allows 5 weekdays either side, which covers a one-session reading difference).
sp500_evidence: For 21 rows the committed Wikipedia changes table (constituents/sp500_changes.csv, pinned revision 1385951946) records the name's removal or addition. Five (BSC, WM, ENE, WCOM, MER) left before the table's coverage and are not in it; their S&P 500 membership is the general record and is not separately sourced here.
chosen: The spec names six (Lehman, Bear Stearns, Washington Mutual, Silicon Valley Bank, First Republic, Bed Bath & Beyond). The other twenty avoid tickers known to have been reused by another listed company (e.g. Wachovia's WB is Weibo's, Monsanto's MON a SPAC's, the old GM's GM the new GM's), since the test fails a code whose series runs on past the date. WM itself is now Waste Management's ticker: a vendor that keeps Washington Mutual under WM.US passes, one that serves Waste Management under it fails, which is the check working.
